subject: Production impact — dedicated pool saturation and error spike (Clearsky)
messages:
From: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@clearsky.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production delays and 5xx errors this morning

Sofia —

We started seeing elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors against the inference endpoints attached to our Reserved capacity at ~08:45 PDT. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side (steady batch inference). Error rate climbed to ~12% and median latency moved from ~85ms to ~420ms. Our engineers captured traces and a short error log (attached).

This is causing failed transactions for some customers — we need an immediate mitigation plan (fallback to hosted variant, potential burst, or any short-term patch). We also need clarity on whether our reserved pool is being saturated by noisy neighbors or if some internal autoscale behavior is mis-routing.

Please advise next steps and an ETA for a fix. If you need an emergency bridge, we can join now.

— Samantha
Samantha Yu
Head of Infrastructure, Clearsky AI
Samantha.Yu@clearsky.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production delays and 5xx errors this morning

Quick summary after looking at telemetry:
- Dedicated pool for CLRSKY (pool id: dp-73b) shows sustained queue depth increase starting 08:42 PDT. GPU utilization is high on 6 of 8 hosts; KV cache eviction rate spiked, causing repeated cold-cache token recomputation.
- The error pattern is 502/504 from the interop proxy layer when the request waits past the router timeout (we have a small window where requests are dropped to protect latency SLAs for other customers). That explains the sudden 5xx fraction.
- Root cause candidates: a) a sudden large batch submission from one of their clients, or b) noisy neighbor on the cluster (cross-tenant oversubscription).

Immediate mitigations executed (09:30 — 09:34):
- Enabled emergency prefix caching for the most common prompt IDs (reduces recompute pressure).
- Temporarily bumped their routing priority to the reserved fallback lane (adds ~5% cost but reduces queuing).
- Provisioned a small burst window (30 minutes) from a shared pool — pending approval for continued authorization.

Next steps:
- Ops (Marissa): confirm whether the shared pool has contiguous headroom to extend a 2-hour burst. If not, we need an exec sign-off to reallocate capacity.
- Sales (Sofia): ask Clearsky for any anomalous traffic from their side (batch jobs / spikes) and request sample request IDs.

I will keep monitoring and will post telemetry snippets to the HS ticket.

— Priyom
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production delays and 5xx errors this morning

Quick ops readout — current state at 10:05 PDT:
- Shared-burst pool has ~12% immediate headroom (enough for a 45-minute temporary window at current traffic).
- No scheduled maintenance or autoscaler changes in the cluster event logs for the last 6 hours.
- We observed two non-CLRSKY tenants with atypical spike patterns; we throttled them at the infra layer which freed up ~8% capacity and dropped error rates to ~3% for Clearsky.

Recommendation and ask:
- Approve a 2-hour burst authorization for CLRSKY (manual reallocation + billing note) to stabilize while they investigate origin of their batch spike. If leadership prefers, we can offer a one-time service credit in lieu of extended burst.
- I will keep the temporary routing bump in place; we should preserve their Reserved perf profile after the window.

Sofia — please propose language for the customer update (clear, apology, mitigation summary, and what we will do next).

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
